title: cost-opt: autotune defaults for batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
description:
Context: This PR centralizes and automates three closely related cost-optimization areas: (1) sensible defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, (2) quantization profile selection and safe fallbacks, and (3) unit-economics tooling surfaced in the Console and CLI. Motivation: many customers run suboptimal configs (too-small batches, disabled prefix cache, conservative quantization) which increases per-token cost. This change aims to provide safe defaults + an autotune path that can be enabled per-deployment to reduce ops friction and drive unit-cost savings. Checklist:
- [x] implement autotune service that collects per-route latency/cost signals and proposes config deltas
- [x] introduce minimally-invasive batching/caching defaults at the router + runtime layer
- [x] add quantization profile selection with runtime compatibility checks and automated rollback
- [x] expose unit-econ dashboard widgets and CLI commands for cost delta simulation
- [x] add end-to-end tests and benchmarks + release notes
What changed (summary):
- runtime: new config knobs and default policy files (runtime/batching_defaults.go, runtime/cache_defaults.go) that apply conservative max_batch_size/max_batch_latency and enable prefix KV caching for compatible models. Defaults are opt-out for Dedicated/Private via env flags.
- autotune: new service (autotune/agent) that samples request traces, computes marginal cost/latency curves, and writes suggested changes to a proposals API. Proposals are automatically applied when confidence thresholds are met.
- quant: quant-profile registry (models/quant_profiles.json) + runtime checks to ensure a quantized kernel is compatible; fallback to fp16 if a profile fails fast path.
- console: new Unit Economics panel and CLI commands (redwood cost simulate / redwood cost apply) that show estimated monthly savings and risk (latency delta percentile).
- telemetry: new metrics (cost_savings_suggested, autotune_proposals_applied, quant_profile_fallbacks) and alerts for >1% p95 latency regression post-apply.
Performance / impact: In internal canary runs across 10 customer-like workloads we observed median 28% unit-cost reduction (15-48% range) with negligible p95 latency regression (<2.5% in guarded rollouts). Cost savings are primarily from larger effective batching and enabling KV prefix caching; quantization provided additional gains on large models (6-18%) when compatible. Migration & rollout notes: defaults are enabled for hosted API immediately. Dedicated and Private deployments remain opt-out until the admin flag is set to enable autotune. Autotune proposals go through a simulated dry-run on a production-like shadow path before being scheduled for rollouts. Related: ENG-3214 (autotune service), ENG-3267 (quantization profiles), SUP-4421 (customer requests to reduce token spend).
